title: What If the Ocean Kept Getting More Acidic?

scenes.text: What if the ocean kept turning acidic? Its tiniest swimmers would feel it first.
The ocean absorbs about 30 percent of our carbon dioxide, and surface water is already about 30 percent more acidic.
Acid eats at carbonate, the mineral that shells and coral skeletons are made of.
In lab tests at projected 2100 levels, the shells of tiny sea snails called pteropods slowly dissolved over 45 days.
Oysters and corals struggle to build at all, and heavy shell damage is already documented in the Southern Ocean.
Pteropods are food for fish, so the smallest shell in the sea holds up a lot of the food web.
